| R-01 | Major | src/stock/stock-repository.ts > buildAdjustment (positive-delta branch); src/stock/stock-validation.ts > adjustStockSchema; src/items/item.ts > toItem | A positive adjustment has no upper bound. `delta` may be any safe integer, and an increment checks only `attribute_exists(sku)`, so `quantity + delta` can go past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (for example an item at 1 adjusted by +9007199254740991). DynamoDB stores the bigger number and commits the write. The document client then reads it back as a BigInt (or with lost precision), `toItem` throws CorruptItemRecord, and the caller gets a 500 for a change that was already saved. From then on, every GET of that SKU, every list page that includes it, and every later adjustment returns 500 until someone fixes the record by hand. The API is public and unauthenticated (OQ-1), so any anonymous caller can do this with one request. No test covers it. | For increments, add an upper-bound condition, `quantity <= :maxAllowed` with `:maxAllowed = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - delta`, and map its failure to a 4xx (a ValidationError, or a documented 409). Otherwise, cap `delta` and `quantity` at a documented maximum in validation. Add a repository integration test showing an overflowing increment is rejected and the stored quantity is unchanged. | New |

### Summary

The core risk is handled. Stock adjustment is a single conditional `UpdateItem`, and the mandatory race test passes on DynamoDB Local with no lost updates and the zero floor holding. Layering, dependency injection, the single error envelope, boundary validation, strict TypeScript, and the lint, format and type-check gates are all confirmed. The one real defect is an unbounded increment: one anonymous request can save a quantity past the safe-integer range and leave that item returning 500 permanently. Fix it before release. The other findings are about accurate evidence and documentation.
